avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin (if used concurrently)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive anticoagulant effects significantly increase bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; coordinate anticoagulation therapy with prescriber

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potentiates antiplatelet and anticoagulant effects, increases bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin E supplementation to <400 IU/day; monitor for bleeding signs

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Inhibits platelet aggregation and may potentiate anticoagulant effects
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid supplement; counsel patient on bleeding risk

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic (concentrated supplements)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Antiplatelet activity compounds heparin's anticoagulant effects
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue concentrated garlic supplements; food amounts are acceptable

avoid_supplements.name: Ginseng
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May reduce anticoagulant effect and increase thrombotic risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid use; monitor INR/aPTT if inadvertently used

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May reduce heparin effectiveness through unknown mechanisms
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid supplement; counsel on interaction risk

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (fish oil)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet effects; additive with heparin at high doses
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for bleeding; dose up to 3g/day generally acceptable with monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric/Curcumin
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet activity may slightly potentiate anticoagulation
caution_supplements.action: Monitor patient; culinary amounts safe; monitor with concentrated supplements

caution_supplements.name: Bromelain
caution_supplements.mechanism: Proteolytic enzyme may have mild anticoagulant effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for signs of bleeding; generally low risk at standard doses

avoid_foods.name: Inconsistent Vitamin K intake
avoid_foods.mechanism: While heparin is not vitamin K-dependent, erratic intake affects monitoring stability if patient transitions to warfarin; affects lab interpretation
avoid_foods.action: Maintain consistent daily vitamin K intake; counsel on leafy greens consistency

caution_foods.name: Alcohol (excessive consumption)
caution_foods.mechanism: Alcohol potentiates anticoagulant effects and increases bleeding risk; impairs platelet function
caution_foods.action: Limit to ≤1-2 drinks/day; counsel on moderation

caution_foods.name: Cranberry juice (large quantities)
caution_foods.mechanism: May potentiate anticoagulant effects through unknown mechanism
caution_foods.action: Moderate intake; monitor for bleeding if consuming >1L daily

monitoring_notes: Heparin is a non-hepatically metabolized anticoagulant, so CYP interactions are minimal; primary concerns are additive antiplatelet/anticoagulant effects from supplements and foods. Monitor aPTT regularly and observe for signs of bleeding (ecchymosis, hematuria, epistaxis, melena); educate patients on the critical importance of disclosing all supplements and herbs.
